greek: Καὶ Μωυσῇ εἶπεν Ἀνάβηθι πρὸς κύριον σὺ καὶ Ααρων καὶ Ναδαβ καὶ Αβιουδ καὶ ἑβδομήκοντα τῶν πρεσβυτέρων Ισραηλ, καὶ προσκυνήσουσιν μακρόθεν τῷ κυρίῳ·
hint: Moses is told to come up with Aaron, Nadab, Abihu and seventy elders, who are to bow down from a distance.

notes.text: Said, with no subject named; the speaker is the lord of 23:20–33.
ἑβδομήκοντα, seventy, one translation, plain text.

reading: And to [[name:Μωυσῇ]] [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[go up|go up, mount, ascend, go up to, rise, come up, come to and arrive at, go up country, go aboard|ἀναβαίνω]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] [[lord|lord, master, the one having power and authority over|κύριος]] you and [[name:Ααρων]] and [[name:Ναδαβ]] and [[name:Αβιουδ]] and seventy [[of the elders|of the elders, of the older, of the higher and more important, of the greater than, of the elders of the Jewish Council, of the elders of the Church and presbyters|πρεσβύτερος]] of [[name:Ισραηλ]], and [[they will make obeisance|they will make obeisance, they will fall down and worship and worship and adore, they will do reverence to, they will make the salam, they will prostrate themselves before|προσκυνέω]] [[from afar|from afar, from long since|μακρόθεν]] [[to the lord|to the lord, to the master, to the one having power and authority over|κύριος]];

names.gloss: (Μωυσῆς, from Hebrew Mōšeh, which the Hebrew of 2:10 hears in māšâ, "to draw out")
(Ααρων, from Hebrew ʾAhărōn, of uncertain meaning)
(Αβιουδ, from Hebrew ʾĂbîhûʾ, "he is my father")
(Ισραηλ, from Hebrew Yiśrāʾēl, which the Hebrew of Genesis 32:29 hears in śārâ ʿim ʾĕlōhîm, "he strove with God")

greek: καὶ ἐγγιεῖ Μωυσῆς μόνος πρὸς τὸν θεόν, αὐτοὶ δὲ οὐκ ἐγγιοῦσιν· ὁ δὲ λαὸς οὐ συναναβήσεται μετʼ αὐτῶν.
hint: Moses alone is to come near God; the others are not, and the people do not go up.

notes.text: ἐγγίζω, the Attic future, ἐγγιῶ.
συναναβαίνω, to go up with, one translation, plain text.
The article cut off from its noun by δέ, which goes first.

reading: and [[will bring near|will bring near and bring up to, will approach, will be imminent, will approximate to, will be next of kin, will be on the point of|ἐγγίζω]] [[name:Μωυσῆς]] [[alone|alone, left alone and forsaken and solitary, only|μόνος]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] [[the God|him who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only|θεός]], they [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], not [[they will bring near|they will bring near and bring up to, they will approach, they will be imminent, they will approximate to, they will be next of kin, they will be on the point of|ἐγγίζω]]; [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[the people|the people, the men, the soldiers, the land-army, the common men, the folk, the Jews, the Christians|λαός]] not will go up with [[in the midst of|in the midst of, among, in common, along with, with, by means of|μετά + genitive]] of them.

greek: εἰσῆλθεν δὲ Μωυσῆς καὶ διηγήσατο τῷ λαῷ πάντα τὰ ῥήματα τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ τὰ δικαιώματα· ἀπεκρίθη δὲ πᾶς ὁ λαὸς φωνῇ μιᾷ λέγοντες Πάντας τοὺς λόγους, οὓς ἐλάλησεν κύριος, ποιήσομεν καὶ ἀκουσόμεθα.
hint: Moses tells the people the words and ordinances; with one voice they answer that they will do and hear all of it.

notes.text: Answered, singular, with all the people; saying, plural, by sense.
We will do and hear: the Hebrew of this verse has only naʿăśeh, we will do; the Greek adds the hearing, as the Hebrew does at 24:7.

greek: καὶ ἔγραψεν Μωυσῆς πάντα τὰ ῥήματα κυρίου. ὀρθρίσας δὲ Μωυσῆς τὸ πρωὶ ᾠκοδόμησεν θυσιαστήριον ὑπὸ τὸ ὄρος καὶ δώδεκα λίθους εἰς τὰς δώδεκα φυλὰς τοῦ Ισραηλ·
hint: Moses writes down the words, then at dawn builds an altar below the mountain and twelve stones for the twelve tribes.

notes.text: γράφω, whose first sense is to scratch, scrape, graze; to write is its third. The middle's and passive's senses are left to those voices.
θυσιαστήριον, an altar, one translation, plain text.
The article over an adverb carries its noun as plain text, the thing, neuter.
Twelve stones: the Hebrew has maṣṣēbâ, pillars.

[[having risen early|having risen early and been awake early|ὀρθρίζω]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[name:Μωυσῆς]] the thing [[early in the day|early in the day, early, at morn, betimes, in good time, too soon and too early|πρωΐ]] [[built a house|built a house, built, built for himself|οἰκοδομέω]] an altar [[towards and under|towards and under, under and into, under and before, under, in subjection, towards, about, about the time, to a certain degree and in some measure|ὑπό + accusative]] [[the mountain|the mountain and hill|ὄρος]] and twelve [[stones|stones, precious stones, marbles|λίθος]] [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] the twelve [[races|races, tribes, bodies united by ties of blood and descent, clans, tribes by local habitation, hundreds and counties, contingents furnished by a tribe, brigades|φυλή]] of the [[name:Ισραηλ]];

greek: καὶ ἐξαπέστειλεν τοὺς νεανίσκους τῶν υἱῶν Ισραηλ, καὶ ἀνήνεγκαν ὁλοκαυτώματα καὶ ἔθυσαν θυσίαν σωτηρίου τῷ θεῷ μοσχάρια.
hint: Young men of Israel offer whole burnt offerings and sacrifice calves to God.

notes.text: νεανίσκος, a youth, one translation, plain text.
An offering of deliverance, σωτήριος used as a noun, its first noun sense, for the Hebrew zĕbāḥîm šĕlāmîm.
μοσχάριον, little calf, one translation, plain text; in apposition to the offering, for the Hebrew pārîm, bulls.

reading: and [[sent quite away|sent quite away, dispatched|ἐξαποστέλλω]] the youths of the sons of [[name:Ισραηλ]], and [[brought up|brought up, carried up, carried up the country, took with them, poured forth, heaved and uttered, upheld and took upon themselves, offered and contributed, led up, carried back and recovered, brought back and reported, traced up|ἀναφέρω]] [[whole burnt-offerings|whole burnt-offerings and holocausts|ὁλοκαύτωμα]] and [[offered|offered, burned, sacrificed, slaughtered and slew, offered sacrifices, celebrated with offerings|θύω]] [[an offering|an offering, a mode of offering, offerings and sacrifices and sacred rites, a festival, the victim|θυσία]] [[of deliverance|of deliverance and safety, of thankoffering for deliverance|σωτήριος]] [[to the God|to him who is God definitively, to the one the article marks out, to the known and the only|θεός]] little calves.

greek: λαβὼν δὲ Μωυσῆς τὸ ἥμισυ τοῦ αἵματος ἐνέχεεν εἰς κρατῆρας, τὸ δὲ ἥμισυ τοῦ αἵματος προσέχεεν πρὸς τὸ θυσιαστήριον.
hint: Half the blood goes into bowls, the other half is poured against the altar.

notes.text: ἥμισυς, half, the neuter used as a noun; half of with a genitive; one half.
ἐγχέω, the aorist active; the middle's to fill one's cup left to the middle, and the phrase to fill the κλεψύδρα set aside.
προσχέω, to pour to or on, restored whole.

greek: καὶ λαβὼν τὸ βιβλίον τῆς διαθήκης ἀνέγνω εἰς τὰ ὦτα τοῦ λαοῦ, καὶ εἶπαν Πάντα, ὅσα ἐλάλησεν κύριος, ποιήσομεν καὶ ἀκουσόμεθα.
hint: Moses reads the book of the covenant aloud; the people promise to do and hear all the lord has said.

notes.text: ἀναγινώσκω, filed as ἀναγιγνώσκω: to know well, know certainly, and of written characters to know them again, and so to read. The Ionic first aorist's to persuade is left to that form.
βιβλίον, a paper, scroll, letter, one translation.

greek: λαβὼν δὲ Μωυσῆς τὸ αἷμα κατεσκέδασεν τοῦ λαοῦ καὶ εἶπεν Ἰδοὺ τὸ αἷμα τῆς διαθήκης, ἧς διέθετο κύριος πρὸς ὑμᾶς περὶ πάντων τῶν λόγων τούτων.
hint: Moses sprinkles the people with the blood, naming it the blood of the covenant the lord has made.

notes.text: κατασκεδάννυμι with a genitive, scattered of the people, as Middle Liddell gives τί τινος.
Lo the blood, nominative after ἰδού.

greek: Καὶ ἀνέβη Μωυσῆς καὶ Ααρων καὶ Ναδαβ καὶ Αβιουδ καὶ ἑβδομήκοντα τῆς γερουσίας Ισραηλ
hint: Moses, Aaron, Nadab, Abihu and seventy of the elders go up.

notes.text: γερουσία, a Council of Elders, Senate, for the Hebrew ziqnê, the elders of; Rahlfs prints no stop after Ισραηλ.

reading: And [[went up|went up, mounted, ascended, went up to, rose, came up, came to and arrived at, went up country, went aboard|ἀναβαίνω]] [[name:Μωυσῆς]] and [[name:Ααρων]] and [[name:Ναδαβ]] and [[name:Αβιουδ]] and seventy [[of the Council of Elders|of the Council of Elders and Senate|γερουσία]] of [[name:Ισραηλ]]

greek: καὶ εἶδον τὸν τόπον, οὗ εἱστήκει ἐκεῖ ὁ θεὸς τοῦ Ισραηλ· καὶ τὰ ὑπὸ τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ ὡσεὶ ἔργον πλίνθου σαπφείρου καὶ ὥσπερ εἶδος στερεώματος τοῦ οὐρανοῦ τῇ καθαριότητι.
hint: They see the place where the God of Israel stood, and beneath his feet something like sapphire brickwork, clear as the sky.

ἵστημι, the pluperfect: had been set and stood so.
The article over a phrase carries its noun, the things; a verbless clause after Rahlfs's high stop.
πλίνθος, a brick, one translation, plain text.

greek: καὶ τῶν ἐπιλέκτων τοῦ Ισραηλ οὐ διεφώνησεν οὐδὲ εἷς· καὶ ὤφθησαν ἐν τῷ τόπῳ τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ ἔφαγον καὶ ἔπιον.
hint: Of Israel's chosen not one is missing; they appear in God's place and eat and drink.

notes.text: Not even one was dissonant, διαφωνέω: the Hebrew has lōʾ šālaḥ yādô, he did not lay his hand on them.

greek: καὶ εἶπεν κύριος πρὸς Μωυσῆν Ἀνάβηθι πρός με εἰς τὸ ὄρος καὶ ἴσθι ἐκεῖ· καὶ δώσω σοι τὰ πυξία τὰ λίθινα, τὸν νόμον καὶ τὰς ἐντολάς, ἃς ἔγραψα νομοθετῆσαι αὐτοῖς.
hint: The lord summons Moses up the mountain to receive stone tablets, the law and the commandments written for the people.

notes.text: πυξίον, a tablet of box-wood, and λίθινος, of stone, one translation each, plain text; the second article over the adjective.

εἰμί, the present imperative, be.

greek: καὶ ἀναστὰς Μωυσῆς καὶ Ἰησοῦς ὁ παρεστηκὼς αὐτῷ ἀνέβησαν εἰς τὸ ὄρος τοῦ θεοῦ·
hint: Moses and Joshua, his attendant, set out and go up the mountain of God.

notes.text: The one having stood by him, the perfect participle of παρίστημι, for the Hebrew mĕšārĕtô, his attendant.
They went up, plural: the Hebrew has wayyaʿal mōšeh, Moses went up.

reading: and [[having stood up|having stood up, having risen, having risen to fight against, having risen to go and set out|ἀνίστημι]] [[name:Μωυσῆς]] and [[name:Ἰησοῦς]] [[the one having stood by|the one having stood by and beside and near and standing so, the one having helped and defended and standing so, the one having come and been at hand and been present and standing so, the one having been near and at hand and standing so, the one having come to the side of and come over to and standing so, the one having come to terms and surrendered and submitted and standing so, the one having happened and standing so, the one having come into its head and occurred to and standing so|παρίστημι]] to him [[went up|went up, mounted, ascended, went up to, rose, came up, came to and arrived at, went up country, went aboard|ἀναβαίνω]] [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[the mountain|the mountain and hill|ὄρος]] [[of the God|of him who is God definitively, of the one the article marks out, of the known and the only|θεός]];

greek: καὶ τοῖς πρεσβυτέροις εἶπαν Ἡσυχάζετε αὐτοῦ, ἕως ἀναστρέψωμεν πρὸς ὑμᾶς· καὶ ἰδοὺ Ααρων καὶ Ωρ μεθʼ ὑμῶν· ἐάν τινι συμβῇ κρίσις, προσπορευέσθωσαν αὐτοῖς.
hint: The elders are told to wait while the two are away; Aaron and Hur are with them for any dispute.

greek: καὶ ἀνέβη Μωυσῆς καὶ Ἰησοῦς εἰς τὸ ὄρος, καὶ ἐκάλυψεν ἡ νεφέλη τὸ ὄρος.
hint: Moses and Joshua go up, and the cloud covers the mountain.

notes.text: Moses and Joshua went up: the Hebrew names Moses alone.

reading: and [[went up|went up, mounted, ascended, went up to, rose, came up, came to and arrived at, went up country, went aboard|ἀναβαίνω]] [[name:Μωυσῆς]] and [[name:Ἰησοῦς]] [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[the mountain|the mountain and hill|ὄρος]], and [[covered with|covered with, covered, covered and grasped, buried, covered and concealed, covered with dishonour and threw a cloud over, put over as a covering|καλύπτω]] [[the cloud|the cloud, the bird-net|νεφέλη]] [[the mountain|the mountain and hill|ὄρος]].

greek: καὶ κατέβη ἡ δόξα τοῦ θεοῦ ἐπὶ τὸ ὄρος τὸ Σινα, καὶ ἐκάλυψεν αὐτὸ ἡ νεφέλη ἓξ ἡμέρας· καὶ ἐκάλεσεν κύριος τὸν Μωυσῆν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ ἑβδόμῃ ἐκ μέσου τῆς νεφέλης.
hint: The glory of God rests on Sinai for six days; on the seventh the lord calls Moses from the cloud.

notes.text: Stepped down: the Hebrew has wayyiškōn, and it dwelt.
δόξα, a notion, opinion, and the estimation of others, glory; Middle Liddell's first sense heads.

greek: τὸ δὲ εἶδος τῆς δόξης κυρίου ὡσεὶ πῦρ φλέγον ἐπὶ τῆς κορυφῆς τοῦ ὄρους ἐναντίον τῶν υἱῶν Ισραηλ.
hint: To the Israelites the glory looks like burning fire on the summit.

notes.text: The article cut off from its noun by δέ, which goes first; a verbless clause.
φλέγω, the present active participle, neuter with fire; the passive's senses left to the passive.

greek: καὶ εἰσῆλθεν Μωυσῆς εἰς τὸ μέσον τῆς νεφέλης καὶ ἀνέβη εἰς τὸ ὄρος καὶ ἦν ἐκεῖ ἐν τῷ ὄρει τεσσαράκοντα ἡμέρας καὶ τεσσαράκοντα νύκτας.
hint: Moses enters the cloud and stays on the mountain forty days and forty nights.

notes.text: Was, the imperfect of εἰμί, with the formula.
τεσσαράκοντα, forty, one translation, plain text.
